# Yama walks into a insurance & protection services firm

The insurance & protection services world does not cite Yama in its documentation. It does not need to — it performs the archetype daily, unbilled.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Twin Dialogue.** The oldest Yama-text is a dialogue: Yama and his twin Yamī, the first two beings, and Yamī’s love for her brother.  Yama refuses — ‘the immortals watch’ — and the hymn becomes the charter of exogamy and of the incest-taboo itself, argued between the world’s first twins in the world’s first debate.

**The Path of the Fathers.** The funeral hymn sends the dead king along the path Yama blazed, past the two dogs and the waters, to the feast of the fathers where Yama waits with Varuṇa.  ‘Leave the sin here, keep the glory’ — the formula of every Vedic funeral, spoken to the first traveller’s successor.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Insurance & Protection Services

*The judge whose account never errs — the final audit every policy eventually faces.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Legal, Justice & Compliance

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *The first mortal who became the judge of all — his noose finds every soul at its hour.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Yama was always going to be re-derived wherever death, justice, underworld matters.

### Ancestry & Heritage Services

*King of the ancestral world — the fathers' realm he rules is genealogy's destination.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

## Not the First Rebrand

The Avestan Yima, king of the golden age who kept death from his realm, is Yama’s Iranian twin — the same name, opposite function: where Yima postponed death, Yama administers it.  Buddhism made Yama a dharmapāla, converted in the end by the Buddha’s teaching, and carried him east as Enma in Japan, where he still judges with his mirror and staff. The office is only the latest translation.
